theory.intro: The **surface area** of a prism is the total area of all its faces, which is the area of its net. Find the area of every face and add them. A right prism has two identical end faces plus one rectangle per side of them.
facts: For a right-angled or isosceles triangular face, a slant edge is often not given — find it with Pythagoras' theorem before working out the rectangles.
An **open** container (no lid) leaves one face off, so add only the faces that are actually there.
Keep every length in the same unit; surface area is in square units ($\text{cm}^{2}$, $\text{m}^{2}$).
steps: Identify every face of the prism.
If a slant edge is unknown, find it using Pythagoras' theorem.
Find the area of each face.
Add the areas of all the faces.

workedExamples.question_text: Calculate the surface area of a closed rectangular prism measuring $9\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$ by $2\text{ cm}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Front and back:
$\begin{align*}A_1&=(9\times2)\times2\\&=36\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Sides:
$\begin{align*}A_2&=(5\times2)\times2\\&=20\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Top and bottom:
$\begin{align*}A_3&=(9\times5)\times2\\&=90\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{SA}&=36+20+90\\&=146\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: Calculate the surface area of a cube with side length $3\text{ cm}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:

$\begin{align*}\text{SA}&=6\times3^2\\&=6\times9\\&=54\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A_1&=2\times\frac12\times8\times6\\&=48\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A_1&=2\times\frac12\times12\times8\\&=96\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}A_2&=12\times9\\&=108\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Two equal side rectangles:
$\begin{align*}A_3&=(10\times9)\times2\\&=180\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{SA}&=96+108+180\\&=384\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: An open box has a rectangular base $10\text{ cm}$ by $7\text{ cm}$ and height $3\text{ cm}$. Calculate the total area of its five faces.
workedExamples.solution_text:
There is no lid. Count the base and four sides.
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{base}}&=10\times7=70\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{long sides}}&=(10\times3)\times2=60\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{short sides}}&=(7\times3)\times2=42\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{SA}&=70+60+42\\&=172\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

Two trapezium ends:
$\begin{align*}A_1&=2\times\frac12(14+8)\times4\\&=88\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Bottom, top and two sloping rectangles:
$\begin{align*}A_2&=14\times7=98\text{ cm}^2\\A_3&=8\times7=56\text{ cm}^2\\A_4&=(5\times7)\times2=70\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{SA}&=88+98+56+70\\&=312\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A book measures $22\text{ cm}$ by $16\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$. Plastic covers all six faces. Find the area needed for $250$ books, in square metres. Ignore overlaps and waste.
workedExamples.solution_text:
For one book:
$\begin{align*}A_1&=(22\times3)\times2=132\text{ cm}^2\\A_2&=(16\times3)\times2=96\text{ cm}^2\\A_3&=(22\times16)\times2=704\text{ cm}^2\\\text{SA}&=132+96+704\\&=932\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
For all books:
$\begin{align*}A&=932\times250\\&=233000\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
Since $1\text{ m}^2=10000\text{ cm}^2$:
$233000\div10000=23.3\text{ m}^2$

workedExamples.question_text: A closed rectangular prism has base dimensions $9\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ and height $x\text{ cm}$. Its surface area is $228\text{ cm}^2$. Find $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Add the two bases and four side faces.
$\begin{align*}228&=2(9\times4)+2(9x)+2(4x)\\228&=72+26x\\26x&=156\\x&=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A closed triangular prism has an isosceles cross-section with base $12\text{ cm}$, perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$ and two sloping sides of $10\text{ cm}$. Its surface area is $288\text{ cm}^2$. Find its length $x\text{ cm}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Two triangular ends:
$A_{\text{ends}}=2\times\frac12\times12\times8=96\text{ cm}^2$
The three rectangles have areas $12x$, $10x$ and $10x$.
$\begin{align*}288&=96+12x+10x+10x\\288&=96+32x\\32x&=192\\x&=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A closed rectangular storage crate measures $1.2\text{ m}$ by $1\text{ m}$ by $0.5\text{ m}$. All six faces are painted. A tin covers $2\text{ m}^2$ and costs $\$9$. Find the total cost of the tins needed.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}A_1&=(1.2\times0.5)\times2=1.2\text{ m}^2\\A_2&=(1\times0.5)\times2=1\text{ m}^2\\A_3&=(1.2\times1)\times2=2.4\text{ m}^2\\\text{SA}&=1.2+1+2.4\\&=4.6\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$4.6\div2=2.3$
Buy three whole tins.
$\text{Cost}=3\times9=\$27$

development.question_text:

$= 96\text{ cm}^{2}$

$A_3 = (24\times 18)\times 2$
$= 864\text{ cm}^{2}$

$= 1032\text{ cm}^{2}$
Area of plastic for $500$ books:
$1032\times 500 = 516000\text{ cm}^{2}$
$516000\div 10000 = 51.6\text{ m}^{2}$
